title: What staff training does Dubai's VARA require of virtual asset service providers?
description: What VARA's Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook requires for VASP staff training in Dubai: role training, AML/CFT, anti-bribery, and 30 day onboarding.
shortAnswer: Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA) requires every licensed virtual asset service provider to train staff for their duties at the start of employment and on an ongoing basis, to provide AML/CFT training to all staff regularly, and to communicate all operational policies and procedures to new hires within 30 calendar days. The requirements are in Rule I.J of the Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook, with training duties for the Compliance Officer and MLRO.
keyTakeaways: The Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook forms part of VARA's Virtual Assets and Related Activities Regulations 2023 and applies to all virtual asset service providers (VASPs) licensed by VARA to carry out virtual asset activities in Dubai. Its requirements are binding Rules unless stated otherwise.

Rule I.J.4 requires training suitable for each role at the beginning of employment and on an ongoing basis. Rule I.J.5 requires AML/CFT training for all staff on a regular basis, with monitoring of compliance with procedures.

Rule I.J.6 requires all operational policies and procedures to be communicated to new hires within their first 30 calendar days. Updated policies must be promptly communicated and always available to staff.

The Compliance Officer must ensure staff, including senior management, are trained on all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, including consumer protection and AML/CFT. The MLRO must ensure the board and staff are trained on AML/CFT.
Part VI requires an anti-bribery and corruption training program for the board and all staff on a regular basis, with the policy included in induction for new board members and staff.
appliesTo: Virtual asset service providers (VASPs) licensed by VARA to carry out any virtual asset activity in the Emirate of Dubai
Sponsored VASPs and their Regulated Sponsors under Part VII of the Rulebook
Board members, senior management and all staff of licensed VASPs
Compliance Officers and Money Laundering Reporting Officers (MLROs), who carry personal training responsibilities

sections.heading: Where are VARA's staff training requirements?

blocks.text: VARA's staff training requirements are in the [Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook](https://rulebooks.vara.ae/entiresection/123). VARA was established by Law No. (4) of 2022 Regulating Virtual Assets in the Emirate of Dubai, and the Rulebook is issued under, and forms part of, the Virtual Assets and Related Activities Regulations 2023. It applies to all VASPs licensed by VARA, alongside the Company, Technology and Information, and Market Conduct Rulebooks and the rulebook for each licensed activity.

The Rulebook states that, unless otherwise stated, all of its requirements are Rules and have binding effect. Part I sets general principles, the compliance management system, the Compliance Officer's duties, risk management, records, and "employee management and training". Part III covers anti-money laundering and combating the financing of terrorism (AML/CFT), and Part VI covers anti-bribery and corruption. Capitalized terms such as Staff and Senior Management take their meanings from the Company Rulebook.

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the Rulebook as published on VARA's rulebooks site as at November 2026. VARA amends its rulebooks from time to time, so check the current version before relying on a specific rule number.

sections.heading: What does Rule I.J require for staff management and training?

blocks.text: Rule I.J requires qualified staff, up to date policy information, role based training from day one and on an ongoing basis, regular AML/CFT training for everyone, and a 30 day deadline for communicating operational policies to new hires. The seven rules are summarized below.

blocks.caption: Compliance and Risk Management Rulebook, Rule I.J: Staff Management and Training
head: Rule
Requirement
Training implication
rows: I.J.1
Employ only suitably qualified individuals with the requisite skills, knowledge and expertise, registered with applicable professional bodies
Pre-hire checks of qualifications and registrations; competence evidence at hire
I.J.2
Employ appropriate numbers of staff; staff need not be in Dubai if supervisory, monitoring and enforcement functions are effectively implemented
Training must reach staff in every location
I.J.3
Provide all staff with adequate and up to date information on all policies and procedures
Policy library access and version control
I.J.4
Adequate training suitable for each role's duties at the beginning of employment and on an ongoing basis
Role based curriculum at onboarding plus a refresh plan
I.J.5
AML/CFT training for all staff on a regular basis, and monitoring of compliance with established procedures
Enterprise wide AML/CFT program with a set cycle and compliance monitoring
I.J.6
Communicate all operational policies and procedures to new hires within their first 30 calendar days
Onboarding tracker with a day 30 deadline
I.J.7
When operational policies change, promptly communicate the information to all staff and keep updated versions available at all times
Change notifications and attestations linked to policy versions

blocks.text: The Rulebook does not define "regular basis" or "ongoing basis" as a fixed interval. A VASP should set intervals by role and risk and record why, which is the approach in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

sections.heading: Who is responsible for staff training at a VASP?

blocks.text: Two named officers are accountable. Under Rule I.C.2(a), the Compliance Officer (CO) is responsible for "ensuring Staff, including Senior Management, are properly and adequately trained in respect of their understanding and compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, including those relating to consumer protection and AML/CFT". Under Rule III.A.2(a), the Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO) is responsible for ensuring the board and staff are properly and adequately trained on all applicable AML/CFT laws and regulatory requirements, particularly those relevant to virtual asset activities.

items: The CO must have at least five years of relevant compliance experience, be approved by VARA as fit and proper, be resident in the UAE or hold a UAE passport, be a full time employee, and report directly to the board. The appointment is reviewed annually.

The MLRO must have at least two years of experience handling AML/CFT matters and be fit and proper, with an annual review. The MLRO reports to the board quarterly on the effectiveness of AML/CFT policies and procedures.
Compliance and AML/CFT activities can be delegated, but the CO and MLRO remain accountable for them.
Rule I.B.5 requires all staff performing compliance functions to be fit and proper and to have the necessary skills, qualifications and experience.

blocks.text: Because the CO's duty extends to senior management and the MLRO's to the board, training records need to cover directors and executives, not only operational staff.

sections.heading: What AML/CFT and anti-bribery training is required?

blocks.text: VARA requires AML/CFT training for all staff on a regular basis (Rule I.J.5) and an anti-bribery and corruption program for the board and all staff on a regular basis (Rule VI.D.1). For anti-bribery and corruption, the Rulebook adds that all board members and staff must participate in the training provided, must have access to the current policy and be told of changes (Rule VI.D.2), and that training on the policy should form part of the induction program for new board members and staff (Rule VI.D.3).

AML/CFT training content should follow the VASP's own risk assessment and the controls in Part III, including customer due diligence, ongoing monitoring, suspicious transaction reporting to the MLRO without tipping off, the Travel Rule, sanctions screening, and enhanced controls for anonymity enhanced transactions where offered. VASPs are also subject to federal AML/CFT law, covered in [UAE AML/CFT training requirements](/regulations/uae-aml-cft-training-requirements).

Enforcement action for breaches of Part III may be taken directly against the VASP, its directors, Responsible Individuals, the MLRO and Senior Management (Rule III.J.2). That personal exposure is a practical reason to give board members their own AML/CFT session rather than including them in staff e-learning.

sections.heading: How do VARA's training rules map to evidence?

blocks.text: Rule I.F.1(c) requires VASPs to maintain sufficient records to prove compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements, which includes the training rules. blocks.title: Illustrative 30 day onboarding plan
blocks.text: Day 1: code of conduct, information security, and how to report concerns. Week 1: AML/CFT fundamentals and anti-bribery and corruption policy. By day 30: every remaining operational policy and procedure for the role, acknowledged against the current version, with role training underway. The 30 day deadline comes from Rule I.J.6; the sequence is an example, not a VARA requirement.

sections.heading: How does VARA compare with other UAE regimes?

blocks.text: VARA's rules are shorter and less prescriptive about content than some financial regulators' training regimes, but they add a hard onboarding deadline and personal training duties for the CO and MLRO. Firms licensed in more than one regime can compare the [DFSA training and competence requirements](/regulations/dfsa-training-and-competence-requirements) for the DIFC and keep one core AML/CFT curriculum with regime specific modules. For structuring onboarding across roles, see [how to structure onboarding for regulated roles](/guides/how-to-structure-onboarding-for-regulated-roles).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each VARA rule as an obligation with its audience, deadline and evidence, so the 30 day onboarding rule, the regular AML/CFT cycle and the board level duties are tracked as separate requirements. Learning outcomes and assessment points are defined before content is written, and when VARA amends a rulebook the affected modules can be identified from the framework.

faqs.q: How often must VASP staff complete AML/CFT training under VARA rules?
faqs.a: The Rulebook requires AML/CFT training for all staff "on a regular basis" without setting an interval. A VASP should document its chosen cycle by role and risk, monitor completion, and be able to show the CO and MLRO approved it. Many firms choose at least annual training, with more frequent updates for high risk roles.

faqs.q: Does the 30 day rule mean all training must be finished in 30 days?
faqs.a: Rule I.J.6 requires all operational policies and procedures to be communicated to new hires within their first 30 calendar days. Rule I.J.4 separately requires role training at the beginning of employment and on an ongoing basis. Communicating policies and completing role training are related but distinct, so track both.

faqs.q: Do board members need training under VARA's rules?
faqs.a: Yes. The MLRO must ensure the board and staff are adequately trained on AML/CFT, and the anti-bribery and corruption program must cover the board and all staff, including induction for new board members. The CO's training duty also covers senior management.

faqs.q: Do VASP staff have to be located in Dubai to be trained?
faqs.a: No. Rule I.J.2 says that, unless otherwise stated, staff need not be physically located in the Emirate, provided supervisory, monitoring and enforcement functions are effectively implemented to VARA's satisfaction. Training and its evidence still need to reach every staff member wherever they work.

Rule I.J.1 to I.J.7: qualified staff; staff need not be in the Emirate; up to date policy information; adequate training at beginning of employment and ongoing; AML/CFT training for all staff on a regular basis with compliance monitoring; operational policies communicated to new hires within first 30 calendar days; updates promptly communicated and available

Rule I.C.1 CO: five years experience, fit and proper approved by VARA, UAE resident or passport, full time, reports to board, annual review; Rule I.C.2(a) CO ensures Staff including Senior Management are trained on all applicable laws including consumer protection and AML/CFT; Rule I.B.5 compliance staff fit and proper

Rule III.A.1 MLRO two years AML/CFT experience, fit and proper, annual review; III.A.2(a) MLRO ensures Board and Staff are trained on AML/CFT relevant to VA Activities; III.A.2(f) quarterly board reports; III.A.3 delegation with continued accountability; III.J.2 enforcement against VASP, directors, Responsible Individuals, MLRO and Senior Management

Rule VI.D.1 to VI.D.3: anti-bribery and corruption training programme for the Board and all Staff on a regular basis, all must participate; access to current policy; training on the policy part of induction for new Board members and Staff
Rule I.F.1(c): maintain sufficient records to prove compliance with all applicable laws and regulatory requirements
